title: Relative Risks of Gastric Cancer for Metabolomic Traits (2026 Update)
source_title: Supplementary table 7. Relative risks of gastric cancer for directly measured and genetically predicted metabolomic traits across diverse cohorts
description: Updated comparisons of directly measured and genetically predicted metabolomic traits across UKBB, SIT, MITS, and UGCED cohorts.
notes:
Note: The table summarizes the RRs of GC associated with directly measured and genetically predicted metabolomic traits across the UKBB Discovery, SIT, MITS, and UGCED cohorts. Directly measured metabolic levels refer to circulating metabolomic trait levels quantified using NMR profiling in the UKBB. Genetically predicted levels refer to trait values predicted using CSL-based genetic models and were evaluated consistently across cohorts. Log-relative risks (log-RRs) and corresponding RRs were estimated using cohort-specific regression models. Number of consistent RR estimates across cohorts indicates the number of cohorts in which the direction of association was concordant. The column ‘Association directions’ summarizes the direction of associations for genetically predicted trait levels across cohorts, where “-” denotes an inverse association (RR<1) and “+” denotes a positive association (RR>1). Directions are reported in the fixed order of UKBB, SIT, MITS, and UGCED, separated by vertical bars.

aColumn V indicates the 134 traits exhibiting significant associations with GC incidence in both measured (FDR-q value<0.05) and genetically predicted levels (P-value<0.05) in the UKBB Discovery cohort.
bColumn W indicates the 131 traits exhibiting significant associations with GC incidence in both measured (FDR-q value<0.05) and genetically predicted levels (P-value<0.05) in the UKBB Discovery cohort, with effect direction being consistent in ≥ 3 independent cohorts.

Abbreviation: CSL, causal stable learning; GC, gastric cancer; RR, relative risk; NMR, nuclear magnetic resonance; UKBB, UK Biobank; MITS, Mass Intervention Trial in Linqu, Shandong Province; SIT, Shandong Intervention Trial; UGCED, Upper Gastrointestinal Cancer Early Detection Program
